title: Add auto-rollback dashboards + alert rules (triggered/suppressed/stale monitors) for rollout safety
author: Aisha Bello
description: Context: Redwood rollouts now evaluate SLO signals (latency/error burn-rate + staleness) and can auto-pause/auto-rollback. We need first-class operator visibility and sane alerts before enabling this broadly in production. This PR adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules for auto-rollback outcomes (triggered/paused/suppressed), monitor coverage & staleness, and a per-service rollout health view. Dashboards: (1) Rollout Safety — Overview: shows decision volume and rate, breakdown by service/route/model_version/region/tier, and top suppress reasons; includes a panel for “monitor missing/stale” to catch the most common gap from game day/postmortems. (2) Rollout Safety — Rollout Detail: scoped to rollout_id; shows decision timeline + links to rollout controller logs and SLO monitor ids (via labels). (3) Rollout Safety — Service Health: operators pick service + route; shows request volume, p95/p99, error rate, burn-rate status (fast/slow windows), and decision outcomes overlaid. Alerts: (A) RedwoodAutoRollbackTriggered (severity=page) fires when rollback is executed for a production tier and not suppressed; pages SRE and notifies service channel (routing via labels: service/team). (B) RedwoodAutoRollbackPaused (severity=notify) for auto-pause outcomes (default notify only, per PM MVP). (C) RedwoodAutoRollbackSuppressed (severity=notify) for suppress actions (admin override / suppression window) so oncall can validate intent and duration. (D) RolloutSLOMonitorStale (severity=notify) when the monitor adapter reports stale data for the rollout scope beyond threshold (default 10m) OR the evaluation pipeline hasn’t produced fresh samples; includes staleness reason label (telemetry_lag|adapter_error|no_samples). (E) RolloutSLOMonitorMissing (severity=notify) when a rollout is configured for SLO-driven actions but no eligible monitor exists for the scope (route/model_version/region/tier) for >15m. Notes/guardrails: uses low-cardinality labels only; rollout_id is only used in dashboards (templated via ad-hoc filters) and is NOT used in alert grouping keys to avoid paging storms. Alerts group by service, route, region, customer_tier. Also adds a short README section describing routing + how to validate monitors before enabling auto-rollback (ties to release gating work). Follow-ups: once PR-477 in incident-bot is live everywhere, we can switch the notify-only alerts to Slack-only with deep links; for now we keep Prometheus alerts as the primary signal for oncall and use Slack notifications as secondary.

review_conversation: Allison Grant: Dashboard variables look good, but please avoid alerting on rollout_id directly; we can’t page on high-cardinality labels. Also align naming with the rollouts SLO metrics standard (decision outcome labels).

Aisha Bello (author): Ack. I removed rollout_id from all alert grouping/labels and kept it dashboard-only (ad-hoc filter). Also updated panels to use outcome={rollback|pause|suppress} and suppression_reason per the standard; pushed 3f2b7e1.

Sean Gallagher: Severity: I’m OK paging for actual rollback execution in prod tiers, but auto-pause should be notify-only. Also add an annotation with the suggested first steps + link to the new runbook section (Confluence path is fine).

Aisha Bello (author): Done. Paused is notify-only, triggered rollback is page only when customer_tier!=dev and suppressed!=true. Added annotations with triage steps and links to sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/auto-rollback-on-slo-breach-runbook.json and the incident playbook section; pushed 8a9c0d4.

Logan Wright: For staleness, can we distinguish “no samples” from adapter failing? That helps oncall decide whether to treat as rollout risk vs telemetry outage. Also prefer a longer stale threshold (10m) to avoid noise during brief telemetry delays.

Aisha Bello (author): Added staleness_reason label (telemetry_lag|adapter_error|no_samples) and tuned default threshold to 10m. Also added a separate low-severity alert for adapter_error spikes that routes to #eng-platform-telemetry; pushed 0c1f6aa.

Caleb Johnson: Recording rules should pre-aggregate by service/route/region/tier; avoid model_version unless needed. Some panels were grouping on model_version by default which can get noisy. Suggest making model_version optional via a dashboard toggle.

Aisha Bello (author): Updated recording rules to aggregate without model_version by default; model_version breakdown is now a panel-level optional query and off by default. Also added a dashboard note about cardinality; pushed 5e77b12.
Rafael Mendes: Please include alert routing labels (team/service) so paging goes to the right oncall rotation, and add a “Top affected services (last 24h)” panel to the overview for game day.

Aisha Bello (author): Added routing labels (team, service) to the alerts (team sourced from existing service metadata map in observability-pack), plus Top affected services panel. Also added a short section in docs on how to update service->team mapping; pushed 2db3a3e.
Allison Grant: Approved after last push. This is consistent with the standards and won’t explode cardinality.
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Let’s monitor alert noise closely during staged enablement and adjust if needed.
release_notes: Adds Rollout Safety dashboards and alerting for auto-rollback/pause/suppress outcomes and monitor staleness/missing coverage. Paging only for executed rollbacks in production tiers; others notify-only.
